Śloka 68

श्रुतिसीमन्तसिन्दूरीकृतपादाब्जधूलिका ।
सकलागमसन्दोहशुक्तिसम्पुटमौक्तिका ॥ ६८ ॥

śrutisīmantasindūrīkṛtapādābjadhūlikā |
sakalāgamasandohaśuktisampuṭamauktikā || 68 ||

Names in this śloka

  1. श्रुतिसीमन्तसिन्दूरीकृतपादाब्जधूलिका śruti-sīmanta-sindūrī-kṛta-pādābja-dhūlikā
  2. सकलागमसन्दोहशुक्तिसम्पुटमौक्तिका sakalāgama-sandoha-śukti-sampuṭa-mauktikā

Each half is a single name (289, 290): the Vedas bowing to Her feet, and the scriptures as the shell that holds Her as a pearl.

289श्रुतिसीमन्तसिन्दूरीकृतपादाब्जधूलिकाśruti-sīmanta-sindūrī-kṛta-pādābja-dhūlikā
Sandhi viccheda
  • सीमन्त → सीमन् + अन्त (sīman + anta) — irregular fusion: in the sense 'hair-parting' sīman (its n dropped) + anta gives sīmanta, the second vowel replacing the first (pararūpa; the śakandhu group of words)
  • पादाब्ज → पाद + अब्ज (pāda + abja) — savarṇa-dīrgha: a + a/ā → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ)
Samāsa vigraha

bahuvrīhi (over inner ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa, saptamī-tatpuruṣa and gati-compound layers)

श्रुतीनाम् सीमन्ताः श्रुतिसीमन्ताः; पादौ अब्जे इव पादाब्जे; पादाब्जयोः धूलिका पादाब्जधूलिका; असिन्दूरम् सिन्दूरम् कृता सिन्दूरीकृता; श्रुतिसीमन्तेषु सिन्दूरीकृता पादाब्जधूलिका यस्याः सा श्रुतिसीमन्तसिन्दूरीकृतपादाब्जधूलिका
śrutīnām sīmantāḥ śrutisīmantāḥ; pādau abje iva pādābje; pādābjayoḥ dhūlikā pādābjadhūlikā; asindūram sindūram kṛtā sindūrīkṛtā; śrutisīmanteṣu sindūrīkṛtā pādābjadhūlikā yasyāḥ sā śrutisīmantasindūrīkṛtapādābjadhūlikā

(1) śruti-sīmanta 'the hair-partings of the Vedas', the Vedas pictured as women (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa). (2) pāda-abja 'lotus feet' (feet like lotuses) and …abja-dhūlikā 'the dust of those feet' (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa). (3) sindūrī-kṛta 'made into vermilion', a cvi formation: sindūra + kṛta with a → ī, meaning 'turned into what it was not' (Pāṇini 7.4.32). (4) The whole is a bahuvrīhi: 'She the dust of whose lotus feet is made the vermilion in the hair-partings of the Vedas'.

Sanskrit componentIASTLiteral English meaning
श्रुतिśrutithe Veda (lit. 'what is heard') — √śru 'to hear'
सीमन्तsīmantathe parting of the hair — sīman 'boundary' + anta 'end'
सिन्दूरीsindūrīvermilion (in the cvi form) — sindūra 'vermilion', with ī before √kṛ (cvi)
कृतkṛtamade, turned into — √kṛ, past participle
पादpādafoot
अब्जabjalotus (lit. 'water-born') — ap 'water' + ja 'born'
धूलिकाdhūlikādust, pollen — dhūli + -kā

Complete meaning She the dust of whose lotus feet becomes the vermilion in the hair-parting of the Vedas

Spiritual significance The Vedas, pictured as married women, bow their heads at Her feet so that the dust of Her feet marks their partings like the vermilion of the auspicious wife: the Upaniṣads, the crown of the Veda, rest at Her feet.

290सकलागमसन्दोहशुक्तिसम्पुटमौक्तिकाsakalāgama-sandoha-śukti-sampuṭa-mauktikā
Sandhi viccheda
  • सकलागम → सकल + आगम (sakala + āgama) — savarṇa-dīrgha: a + a/ā → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ)
  • सन्दोह → सम् + दोह (sam + doha) — m becomes anusvāra before a consonant (Pāṇini 8.3.23) and the anusvāra takes the nasal of the following stop's class, n before d (8.4.58 anusvārasya yayi parasavarṇaḥ)
Samāsa vigraha

ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa (over inner karmadhāraya, ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa and rūpaka layers), applied to Her with the feminine -ā

सकलाः आगमाः सकलागमाः; सकलागमानाम् सन्दोहः सकलागमसन्दोहः; शुक्तेः सम्पुटम् शुक्तिसम्पुटम्; सकलागमसन्दोहः एव शुक्तिसम्पुटम् सकलागमसन्दोहशुक्तिसम्पुटम्; तस्य मौक्तिकम् इव सकलागमसन्दोहशुक्तिसम्पुटमौक्तिका
sakalāḥ āgamāḥ sakalāgamāḥ; sakalāgamānām sandohaḥ sakalāgamasandohaḥ; śukteḥ sampuṭam śuktisampuṭam; sakalāgamasandohaḥ eva śuktisampuṭam sakalāgamasandohaśuktisampuṭam; tasya mauktikam iva sakalāgamasandohaśuktisampuṭamauktikā

(1) sakala-āgama 'all the scriptures' (karmadhāraya) and …āgama-sandoha 'their whole mass' (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa). (2) śukti-sampuṭa 'the closed pair of oyster-valves' (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa). (3) The mass of scripture IS that oyster-shell (a karmadhāraya of identification, rūpaka). (4) mauktika 'pearl' is the head, with the shell in the genitive: She is the pearl within; it takes the feminine -ā as applied to Her.

Sanskrit componentIASTLiteral English meaning
सकलsakalaall, entire
आगमāgamascripture, traditional teaching — ā + √gam 'to come': 'what has come down'
सन्दोहsandohathe whole mass, collection — sam + √duh 'to milk': 'what is milked together'
शुक्तिśuktioyster, pearl-oyster
सम्पुटsampuṭathe closed hollow of two valves, a casket — sam + puṭa 'fold'
मौक्तिकाmauktikāpearl — mauktika (from muktā 'pearl'), with the feminine -ā

Complete meaning She who is the pearl within the oyster-shell formed by all the scriptures together

Spiritual significance The scriptures enclose and guard Her as the shell guards the pearl: their whole worth lies in what they hold, and what they hold is She.

Śloka 69

पुरुषार्थप्रदा पूर्णा भोगिनी भुवनेश्वरी ।
अम्बिकाऽनादिनिधना हरिब्रह्मेन्द्रसेविता ॥ ६९ ॥

puruṣārthapradā pūrṇā bhoginī bhuvaneśvarī |
ambikā'nādinidhanā haribrahmendrasevitā || 69 ||

Names in this śloka

  1. पुरुषार्थप्रदा puruṣārtha-pradā
  2. पूर्णा pūrṇā
  3. भोगिनी bhoginī
  4. भुवनेश्वरी bhuvaneśvarī
  5. अम्बिका ambikā
  6. अनादिनिधना anādi-nidhanā
  7. हरिब्रह्मेन्द्रसेविता hari-brahmendra-sevitā

Where the names join in the śloka

  • अम्बिकाऽनादिनिधना → अम्बिका + अनादिनिधना (ambikā + anādinidhanā) — savarṇa-dīrgha: ā + a → ā; the avagraha (ऽ) marks the a absorbed at the start of the next name

Divide ambikā (295) | anādinidhanā (296): the avagraha marks the initial a of anādi, which carries the negation.

Sandhi viccheda

Samāsa vigraha

Inner layer: puruṣa-artha 'the aims of a person' (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa). Outer layer: -pradā 'giving' is the head and governs them as its object.

Outer layer: the participle arcitā 'worshipped' is the head, and the king of kings stands to it in the instrumental as the agent.

  • ब्रह्मादि → ब्रह्म + आदि (brahma + ādi) — savarṇa-dīrgha: a + ā → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ)
  • आद्यानन्द → आदि + आनन्द (ādi + ānanda) — yaṇ: i becomes y before a dissimilar vowel (Pāṇini 6.1.77 iko yaṇ aci)

Samāsa vigraha

svasya ātmā svātmā; svātmanaḥ ānandaḥ svātmānandaḥ; alavaḥ lavaḥ bhūtā lavībhūtā; svātmānandasya lavībhūtā svātmānandalavībhūtā; brahmā ādiḥ yeṣām te brahmādayaḥ; brahmādīnām ānandaḥ brahmādyānandaḥ; brahmādyānandānām santatiḥ brahmādyānandasantatiḥ; svātmānandalavībhūtā brahmādyānandasantatiḥ yasyāḥ sā svātmānandalavībhūtabrahmādyānandasantatiḥ

(1) sva-ātman 'Her own Self' and svātma-ānanda 'the bliss of Her own Self' (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣas; ātman loses its n in composition). (2) lavībhūta 'become a mere particle': lava 'particle' takes the suffix cvi, which turns its a into ī (Pāṇini 7.4.32 asya cvau) and expresses 'becoming what it was not', and it is compounded with bhūta as a gati (1.4.61 ūryādicviḍācaś ca); the bliss of Her Self stands to it in the genitive ('a particle of …'). (3) brahma-ādi 'Brahmā and the others' (bahuvrīhi), brahmādi-ānanda 'their bliss', and …ānanda-santati 'the whole succession of those blisses' (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣas). (4) The whole is a bahuvrīhi describing Her: 'She for whom the whole range of the bliss of Brahmā and the other gods has become a mere particle of the bliss of Her own Self'. santati is feminine, so the name ends in -iḥ.

Spiritual significance The Taittirīya Upaniṣad measures bliss in steps, each a hundredfold the one before, up to the bliss of Brahmā, and all of it is a fraction of the bliss of Brahman; the Bṛhadāraṇyaka says other beings live on a particle of that bliss. Her own bliss is that whole.

Uncertain For an exact half Pāṇini's rule (2.2.2 ardhaṃ napuṃsakam) puts ardha first; here, as often in later usage, it follows in a genitive compound.

  • तमोभेद → तमस् + भेद (tamas + bheda) — final -as before a voiced consonant: s becomes ru (Pāṇini 8.2.66 sasajuṣo ruḥ), ru becomes u after a (6.1.114 haśi ca), and a + u → o by guṇa (6.1.87): -o

  • सन्तति → सम् + तति (sam + tati) — m becomes anusvāra before a consonant (Pāṇini 8.3.23 mo 'nusvāraḥ), which takes the place of articulation of the following stop (8.4.58–59 anusvārasya yayi parasavarṇaḥ): written n before a dental

(2) …tamo-bheda 'the piercing of that darkness' (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa). (3) bhānumad-bhānu 'the rays of the sun' (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa; bhānumat 'possessing rays' is the sun) and …bhānu-santati 'a stream of those rays'. Śloka 91

Names in this śloka

  1. तत्त्वासना tattvāsanā
  2. तत् tat
  3. त्वम् tvam
  4. अयी ayī
  5. पञ्चकोशान्तरस्थिता pañca-kośāntara-sthitā
  6. निःसीममहिमा niḥsīma-mahimā
  7. नित्ययौवना nitya-yauvanā
  8. मदशालिनी mada-śālinī

Where the names join in the śloka

  • तत्त्वमयी → तत् + त्वम् + अयी (tat + tvam + ayī) — no sound change: three names written together (tvam keeps its m before the vowel of ayī). This is Bhāskararāya's division; read as one word, tattvamayī is name 907

Names 425–427 (tat · tvam · ayī) divide the letters tattvamayī into three names and recall the teaching tat tvam asi, 'That thou art'; the single word tattvamayī comes later as name 907. Names 431–433 (into śloka 92) describe Her mada, the rapture of Her bliss.

Sandhi viccheda
  • तत्त्वासना → तत्त्व + आसना (tattva + āsanā) — savarṇa-dīrgha: a + ā → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ)
Samāsa vigraha

bahuvrīhi

तत्त्वानि आसनम् यस्याः सा तत्त्वासना
tattvāni āsanam yasyāḥ sā tattvāsanā

The members are tattva 'principle of reality' and āsana 'seat'; the whole is a bahuvrīhi describing Her: 'She whose seat is the tattvas'. The neuter āsana takes the feminine -ā because the compound qualifies the Goddess.

Sanskrit componentIASTLiteral English meaning
तत्त्वtattvaprinciple of reality, category of existence — tat 'that' + the abstract suffix -tva: lit. 'that-ness', the true nature of a thing

Complete meaning She whose seat is the tattvas, the principles of reality

Spiritual significance In Śrīvidyā the tattvas, from earth up to Śiva, are the throne on which She is enthroned and worshipped; She rests on all of manifest reality and is not contained by it.

Uncertain A second analysis takes āsana as an agent noun from √ās 'to sit': tattveṣu āste 'She who abides in the tattvas'. The bahuvrīhi ('whose seat is the tattvas') is the more natural reading of the compound.

Sandhi viccheda
  • तत्त्वमयी → तत् + त्वम् + अयी (tat + tvam + ayī) — No sound changes here. tat and tvam are simply juxtaposed (t + tv), and the final m of tvam stays m before the vowel of ayī (it becomes anusvāra only before a consonant, Pāṇini 8.3.23 mo 'nusvāraḥ). The same letters read as one word give tattvamayī 'consisting of the tattvas', which is name 907; here Bhāskararāya divides them into three names, tat (425), tvam (426) and ayī (427), as the 1,000-name count requires.

Not a compound.

Spiritual significance In the Upaniṣadic teaching tat tvam asi, 'That thou art' (Chāndogya Upaniṣad 6.8.7), tat denotes brahman; the Bhagavad Gītā (17.23) names brahman as oṃ tat sat. With 426 and 427 this name sets the teaching of identity within the hymn.

Not a compound.
Sanskrit componentIASTLiteral English meaning

Spiritual significance In tat tvam asi the word tvam denotes the individual self (jīva); its identity with tat (425) is the teaching of Advaita. Name 908, tattvamarthasvarūpiṇī, takes up the same pair: She is the meaning of tat and tvam.

Corrected in this edition त्वं → त्वम्. त्वं → त्वम्: a word standing alone ends in m, not anusvāra. (425 tat, 426 tvam, 427 ayī is Bhāskararāya's division of tattvamayī and is kept.)

Sandhi viccheda
  • त्वमयी → त्वम् + अयी (tvam + ayī) — No sound change: the m of tvam stays m before the vowel a of ayī (Pāṇini 8.3.23 makes m anusvāra only before a consonant). Bhāskararāya's division of tattvamayī into tat, tvam and ayī: see name 425.
Samāsa vigraha
Not a compound.
Sanskrit componentIASTLiteral English meaning
अयीayīO! (a loving or earnest call) — an interjection of address; usually written ayi with short i

Complete meaning She who is called upon with the loving cry 'ayī', 'O Mother!'

Spiritual significance Traditionally ayī is the call of a devotee to the Mother, completing the triad tat, tvam, ayī; some read the three names together as echoing tat tvam asi, 'That thou art'.

Uncertain The sense of ayī is not settled. The common interjection of address is ayi with a short i; the long ī here is read either as that particle lengthened or as a feminine form, and the commentarial derivation could not be confirmed here. The rendering follows the usual reading as a call of address.

(1) pañca-kośa 'the five sheaths': a numeral compound, which counts as a dvigu because another member follows (Pāṇini 2.1.51 taddhitārthottarapadasamāhāre ca).   • निलयाऽऽरक्तवर्णा → …निलया + आरक्तवर्णा (…nilayā + āraktavarṇā) — savarṇa-dīrgha: ā + ā → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ); the double avagraha ऽऽ marks the long ā of ārakta that has merged

The section of the seven yoginīs begins: Ḍākinī in the viśuddhi (475–484), Rākiṇī in the anāhata (485–494), Lākinī in the maṇipūra (495–503), Kākinī in the svādhiṣṭhāna (504–513), Sākinī in the mūlādhāra (514–520), Hākinī in the ājñā (521–527) and Yākinī in the sahasrāra (528–534). Name 476 is āraktavarṇā, not raktavarṇā (that is 499).

(1) vadana-eka 'one face', with the numeral placed after the noun, as in vadana-dvaya (487) and vadana-traya (496). (2) The participle samanvitā 'endowed with' is the head and takes it in the instrumental: 'endowed with a single face'.

(1) kālarātri-ādi 'those of whom Kālarātri is the first' (bahuvrīhi with ādi). (2) It qualifies śakti (karmadhāraya). (3) …śakti-augha 'the host of those śaktis' (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa). (4) The participle vṛtā 'surrounded' is the head of the whole and takes the host in the instrumental.

Śloka 110

सर्वौदनप्रीतचित्ता याकिन्यम्बास्वरूपिणी ।
स्वाहा स्वधाऽमतिर्मेधा श्रुतिः स्मृतिरनुत्तमा ॥ ११० ॥

Names in this śloka

  1. सर्वौदनप्रीतचित्ता sarvaudana-prīta-cittā
  2. याकिन्यम्बास्वरूपिणी yākinyambā-svarūpiṇī
  3. स्वाहा svāhā
  4. स्वधा svadhā
  5. अमतिः a-matiḥ
  6. मेधा medhā
  7. श्रुतिः śrutiḥ
  8. स्मृतिः smṛtiḥ
  9. अनुत्तमा an-uttamā

Where the names join in the śloka

  • स्वधाऽमतिर्मेधा → स्वधा + अमतिः + मेधा (svadhā + amatiḥ + medhā) — ā + a → ā (savarṇa-dīrgha, Pāṇini 6.1.101), marked by the avagraha; then the visarga of amatiḥ becomes r before the voiced m (final s → ru, 8.2.66, kept as r after i)
  • स्मृतिरनुत्तमा → स्मृतिः + अनुत्तमा (smṛtiḥ + anuttamā) — visarga after i becomes r before a voiced sound or a vowel (final s → ru, Pāṇini 8.2.66; ru is kept as r, since the change to u applies only after a)

The yoginī section ends with 534. Name 537 is amatiḥ 'ignorance' (svadhā + amatiḥ; the avagraha shows the a), not matiḥ, which is name 445; 537 and 538 (medhā) pair ignorance and wisdom. 535–536 are the sacrificial calls svāhā and svadhā.

puṇyakīrtiḥ puṇyalabhyā puṇyaśravaṇakīrtanā |
pulomajārcitā bandhamocanī bandhurālakā || 111 ||

Names in this śloka

  1. पुण्यकीर्तिः puṇya-kīrtiḥ
  2. पुण्यलभ्या puṇya-labhyā

  5. बन्धमोचनी bandha-mocanī
  6. बन्धुरालका bandhurālakā

Name 545: divide pulomajā + arcitā (Śacī + 'worshipped'). Name 547 reads bandhurālakā here; the old name list had barbarālakā (see the name's variants).

542पुण्यकीर्तिःpuṇya-kīrtiḥ
Sandhi viccheda
No sound change inside the name; the members stand as written.
Samāsa vigraha

bahuvrīhi (over an inner karmadhāraya)

Inner layer: puṇyā kīrtiḥ 'holy fame' (karmadhāraya: the adjective puṇya qualifies kīrti). Outer layer: a bahuvrīhi, 'She whose fame is holy'. The feminine adjective puṇyā returns to its masculine stem puṇya- in the compound (puṃvadbhāva); kīrti, already feminine, is unchanged. The members meet without sound change.

Spiritual significance Her renown itself purifies: traditionally, to speak of Her glory is already an act of merit, which the next two names develop.

puṇya 'merit' stands in the instrumental to the gerundive labhyā 'to be attained': 'attainable by (means of) merit'. labhyā is the head.

Sanskrit componentIASTLiteral English meaning

लभ्याlabhyāto be attained, attainable — √labh 'to obtain' with the gerundive suffix -ya (yat), feminine

Complete meaning She who is attained through merit

Spiritual significance Traditionally, devotion to Her and initiation into Her worship are said to come only as the ripened fruit of merit gathered over many lives.

544पुण्यश्रवणकीर्तनाpuṇya-śravaṇa-kīrtanā
Sandhi viccheda

Samāsa vigraha

bahuvrīhi (over an inner itaretara-dvandva and karmadhāraya)

श्रवणम् च कीर्तनम् च श्रवणकीर्तने; पुण्ये श्रवणकीर्तने यस्याः सा पुण्यश्रवणकीर्तना

(1) śravaṇa 'hearing' and kīrtana 'singing, praising' form a dvandva, 'hearing and praising'. (2) puṇya qualifies the pair: 'meritorious hearing and praising' (karmadhāraya). (3) The whole is a bahuvrīhi: 'She, the hearing (of whom) and the praising (of whom) are meritorious'; the neuter kīrtana takes the feminine -ā. She is the object of the hearing and singing, not their agent.

Sanskrit componentIASTLiteral English meaning
पुण्यpuṇyameritorious, merit-giving
श्रवणśravaṇahearing, listening — √śru 'to hear'

Spiritual significance Śravaṇa and kīrtana head the traditional list of the forms of devotion; simply listening to Her names and singing them is said to yield merit.

Uncertain That Śacī's worship secures Indra's rule is a traditional reading; no single source for it was confirmed here.

Sandhi viccheda
  • बन्धुरालका → बन्धुर + अलका (bandhura + alakā) — savarṇa-dīrgha: a + a → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ)

Inner layer: bandhura 'wavy' qualifies alaka 'lock of hair, curl' (karmadhāraya). Outer layer: a bahuvrīhi, 'She whose locks are wavy'; alaka takes the feminine -ā.

Sanskrit componentIASTLiteral English meaning
बन्धुरbandhurawavy, curving; also lovely

Uncertain The reading itself: this edition follows the verse text (bandhurālakā) where the old name list read barbarālakā; which of the two Bhāskararāya's text adopts could not be confirmed here. The sense is the same either way.

Variants The source's name list reads बर्बरालका barbarālakā (barbara 'curly'); the verse text, followed here, reads बन्धुरालका. Both readings are current in printed editions.

Corrected in this edition बर्बरालका → बन्धुरालका. Name list read बर्बरालका, verse text बन्धुरालका. The verse reading is adopted (bandhura, wavy; barbara, curly — the sense is the same); barbarālakā is recorded as a variant. Flagged for review.

572पराशक्तिःparā-śaktiḥ
Sandhi viccheda

Samāsa vigraha
Not a compound.
Sanskrit componentIASTLiteral English meaning

Had they been compounded as a karmadhāraya, the feminine parā would normally return to the masculine stem (puṃvadbhāva, Pāṇini 6.3.42): para-. The verse text accordingly prints them as two words.

Divide bhālasthā + indradhanuḥprabhā. Names 591–597 (into śloka 120) place Her at four points for meditation: in the head like the moon, at the brow like the rainbow, in the heart like the sun, in the triangle as a lamp.

Sandhi viccheda

As a bahuvrīhi: 'She whose form is the guru', i.e. who takes the form of the teacher. As a karmadhāraya, guru is the adjective 'weighty, venerable, awesome' (feminine gurvī, reduced to guru- by puṃvadbhāva): 'the awe-inspiring form'. mūrti is feminine, so the name has the same form either way.

Spiritual significance In Śrīvidyā the guru is not different from the Goddess and Śiva; it is She who teaches through the guru and who is received through him.

Uncertain Two compound analyses: bahuvrīhi ('whose form is the guru') and karmadhāraya ('the weighty, awesome form'). The meaning follows the first.

Śloka 127

विश्वगर्भा स्वर्णगर्भाऽवरदा वागधीश्वरी ।

viśvagarbhā svarṇagarbhā'varadā vāgadhīśvarī |
dhyānagamyā'paricchedyā jñānadā jñānavigrahā || 127 ||

Names in this śloka

  1. विश्वगर्भा viśva-garbhā
  2. स्वर्णगर्भा svarṇa-garbhā
  3. अवरदा avaradā
  4. वागधीश्वरी vāg-adhīśvarī
  5. ध्यानगम्या dhyāna-gamyā
  6. अपरिच्छेद्या aparicchedyā
  7. ज्ञानदा jñāna-dā
  8. ज्ञानविग्रहा jñāna-vigrahā

Where the names join in the śloka

  • स्वर्णगर्भाऽवरदा → स्वर्णगर्भा + अवरदा (svarṇagarbhā + avaradā) — savarṇa-dīrgha: ā + a → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101); the avagraha (ऽ) marks the absorbed initial a of the next name
  • ध्यानगम्याऽपरिच्छेद्या → ध्यानगम्या + अपरिच्छेद्या (dhyānagamyā + aparicchedyā) — savarṇa-dīrgha: ā + a → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101); the avagraha (ऽ) marks the absorbed initial a of the next name

Both avagrahas mark a name beginning with a-: name 639 is avaradā (not varadā), name 642 is aparicchedyā. Name 640: vāg is the c of vāc voiced before adhīśvarī.

bhūmā rūpam yasyāḥ sā bhūmarūpā

rūpa 'form, nature' is qualified by bhūman 'plenitude' in apposition, and the whole points to the Goddess: 'She whose form is the Plenitude'. bhūman is an n-stem; its n is dropped at the end of a compound member (bhūma-), a morphological change, not sandhi.

Sanskrit componentIASTLiteral English meaning
भूमन्bhūmanplenitude, the Infinite; abundance, manyness — abstract noun from bahu 'much' (bahu becomes bhū, Pāṇini 6.4.158 bahor lopo bhū ca bahoḥ); bhūma- in the compound
रूपाrūpāhaving the form, of the nature — rūpa 'form' with the feminine -ā of the bahuvrīhi

Complete meaning She whose form is the Bhūman, the boundless Plenitude

Spiritual significance The Chāndogya Upaniṣad (7.23–24) teaches that 'the Plenitude (bhūmā) alone is happiness': where one sees nothing else, hears nothing else, knows nothing else, that is the Bhūman. Taking bhūman as 'manyness', the name also means that She is the sum of all that exists.

Uncertain bhūman can mean 'the Infinite' (Chāndogya 7.23–24) or 'manyness, the aggregate'; both are current for this name.

nis 'out, away' stands for nirgata 'gone away', and the whole points to the Goddess: 'She from whom duality has gone', i.e. in whom there is no duality. dvaita takes the feminine -ā of the bahuvrīhi.

Spiritual significance Traditionally: nothing exists beside Her to make a second, so duality has no place in Her nature.

672ब्रह्मात्मैक्यस्वरूपिणीbrahmātmaikya-svarūpiṇī
Sandhi viccheda
  • ब्रह्मात्म → ब्रह्म + आत्म (brahma + ātma) — savarṇa-dīrgha: a + ā → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ)
  • आत्मैक्य → आत्म + ऐक्य (ātma + aikya) — vṛddhi: a + ai → ai (Pāṇini 6.1.88 vṛddhir eci)
Samāsa vigraha

karmadhāraya with the possessive suffix -in (over an inner ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa and dvandva)

ब्रह्म च आत्मा च ब्रह्मात्मानौ; ब्रह्मात्मनोः ऐक्यम् ब्रह्मात्मैक्यम्; ब्रह्मात्मैक्यम् एव स्वरूपम् ब्रह्मात्मैक्यस्वरूपम्; तत् अस्याः अस्ति इति ब्रह्मात्मैक्यस्वरूपिणी
brahma ca ātmā ca brahmātmānau; brahmātmanoḥ aikyam brahmātmaikyam; brahmātmaikyam eva svarūpam brahmātmaikyasvarūpam; tat asyāḥ asti iti brahmātmaikyasvarūpiṇī

(1) brahman and ātman, the absolute and the Self, are joined as a dvandva (both stems lose their final n, a morphological change). (2) aikya 'oneness' takes them in the genitive: 'the oneness of Brahman and the Self' (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa). (3) That oneness is identified with svarūpa 'own nature' (karmadhāraya). (4) The possessive suffix -in (Pāṇini 5.2.115 ata iniṭhanau) makes 'she who has this as her own nature'.

Sanskrit componentIASTLiteral English meaning

Complete meaning She whose very nature is the oneness of Brahman and the Self (Ātman)

Spiritual significance The central teaching of the Upaniṣads (tat tvam asi, ahaṃ brahmāsmi): the Self and Brahman are not two. She is that identity itself, not a union of two things.

Śloka 138

सर्वोपाधिविनिर्मुक्ता सदाशिवपतिव्रता ।

Names in this śloka

  • साध्वी → साधु + ई (sādhu + ī) — yaṇ: u becomes v before a dissimilar vowel (Pāṇini 6.1.77 iko yaṇ aci)

साध्वी is two names in Bhāskararāya's division: 711 sādhu and 712 ī, since sādhvī is already name 128.

  • निर्मुक्ता → निस् + मुक्ता (nis + muktā) — the final s of nis becomes r before a voiced sound (Pāṇini 8.2.66 sasajuṣo ruḥ)
Samāsa vigraha

pañcamī-tatpuruṣa (over an inner karmadhāraya)

(1) sarva-upādhi 'all limiting adjuncts' (karmadhāraya). (2) The participle vinirmuktā 'wholly released' is the head and takes them in the ablative: 'released from all limiting adjuncts'.

Spiritual significance In Vedānta body, mind and name are upādhis that seem to limit pure consciousness; She, as that consciousness, is untouched by all of them.

(1) sadā-śiva 'ever auspicious', the name of the fifth Brahma. (2) pati-vratā 'she whose vow is her husband', the faithful wife (bahuvrīhi). (3) Sadāśiva stands to her in the genitive: 'the faithful wife of Sadāśiva'.

711साधुsādhu
Sandhi viccheda
  • साध्वी → साधु + ई (sādhu + ī) — yaṇ: u becomes v before a dissimilar vowel (Pāṇini 6.1.77 iko yaṇ aci). The surface sādhvī is read by Bhāskararāya as two names, 711 sādhu and 712 ī, because sādhvī as one word would repeat name 128; the junction between them is this sandhi.
Samāsa vigraha
Not a compound.

Spiritual significance Bhāskararāya divides the surface sādhvī into two names so that name 128 (sādhvī) is not repeated: 711 sādhu 'the good' and 712 ī. She is goodness itself, straight and even toward all.

Uncertain Bhāskararāya's own gloss of sādhu could not be checked against a printed Saubhāgyabhāskara; 'equanimity' (the earlier meaning) may reflect it.

Variants Lists that do not follow Bhāskararāya read sādhvī here as one name, repeating name 128.

Sandhi viccheda

Not a compound.

Spiritual significance In Śrīvidyā the long vowel ī is the letter of kāmakalā, the union of Śiva and Śakti that is the seed of creation (compare name 322, kāmakalārūpā); it stands in Her Pañcadaśī mantra.

Sanskrit componentIASTLiteral English meaning

Uncertain kula has several traditional senses here — the senses, the Kaula path, the family of the knower–knowing–known; the reading as 'the senses' follows the earlier meaning.

Samāsa vigraha

(1) caṇḍa-muṇḍa 'Caṇḍa and Muṇḍa' (itaretara-dvandva). (2) caṇḍamuṇḍa-asura 'the demons Caṇḍa and Muṇḍa' (karmadhāraya, the names in apposition to asura). (3) niṣūdinī 'slayer' (agent noun in -in from ni + √sūd) is the head and takes the pair in the genitive.

Sanskrit componentIASTLiteral English meaning

Spiritual significance In the Devī Māhātmya (ch. 7) Kālī, springing from the Goddess's brow, slays Caṇḍa and Muṇḍa, and is then named Cāmuṇḍā.

Sandhi viccheda

Samāsa vigraha

bahuvrīhi (over an inner dvandva and nañ-tatpuruṣa)

(1) a-kṣara 'imperishable' (nañ-tatpuruṣa). (2) kṣara-akṣara 'the perishable and the imperishable' (dvandva). (3) Both are identified with ātman 'self, nature', and the whole points to the Goddess: 'She whose self is both'. ātman with the suffix -ka in a bahuvrīhi gives -ātmikā.

Sanskrit componentIASTLiteral English meaning

Spiritual significance The Bhagavad Gītā (15.16) names two puruṣas, the perishable (all beings) and the imperishable (the unchanging); She is both. Akṣara also means 'letter', so She is the perishable spoken sound and the imperishable syllable.

Names in this śloka

The adverb viśvatas 'on all sides' qualifies mukha 'face', and the whole points to the Goddess: 'She whose faces are on every side'. A bahuvrīhi ending in a word for a body part forms its feminine in -ī.

  • न्यस्त → नि + अस्त (ni + asta) — yaṇ: i becomes y before a dissimilar vowel (Pāṇini 6.1.77 iko yaṇ aci)

bahuvrīhi (over inner ṣaṣṭhī- and saptamī-tatpuruṣas)

rājyasya dhūḥ rājyadhūḥ; mantriṇyām nyastā mantriṇīnyastā; mantriṇīnyastā rājyadhūḥ yayā sā mantriṇīnyastarājyadhūḥ

(1) rājya-dhur 'the yoke of the kingdom' (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa). (2) mantriṇī-nyasta 'placed on the Mantriṇī' (saptamī-tatpuruṣa with the participle; mantriṇī keeps its ī because this is not a karmadhāraya). (3) The whole is a bahuvrīhi with the instrumental yayā: 'She by whom the burden of the kingdom has been placed on the Mantriṇī'. The participle stands first, as is usual in a bahuvrīhi.

Sanskrit componentIASTLiteral English meaning

राज्यrājyakingdom, rule
धूःdhūḥyoke, burden, responsibility — nominative of dhur; the vowel is lengthened before the final r (Pāṇini 8.2.76 rvor upadhāyā dīrgha ikaḥ)

Spiritual significance In the Lalitopākhyāna Mantriṇī (Śyāmalā, Rājaśyāmalā) is Her prime minister and Daṇḍanāthā (Vārāhī) Her commander; the Empress rules through them. Inwardly, the counsel of the mantra governs the devotee's life.

Uncertain Pāṇini 5.4.74 adds the compound-final -a to a compound ending in dhur (…-dhura); the name keeps the bare dhūḥ, a usage also found in epic and Purāṇic Sanskrit. Noted, not a text concern: the verse and the metre support dhūḥ.

निर्गतम् त्रैगुण्यम् यस्याः सा निस्त्रैगुण्या
nirgatam traiguṇyam yasyāḥ sā nistraiguṇyā

nis 'out, away' stands for nirgata 'gone', and the whole points to the Goddess: 'She from whom the three guṇas have gone'. The s of nis stays s before the voiceless t.

Sanskrit componentIASTLiteral English meaning
निस्niswithout, beyond — prefix

790परापराparāparā
Sandhi viccheda
  • परापरा → पर + अपरा (para + aparā) — savarṇa-dīrgha: a + a → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ)
Samāsa vigraha

karmadhāraya (of two co-referential adjectives)

परा च असौ अपरा च परापरा
parā ca asau aparā ca parāparā

parā 'supreme' and aparā 'not supreme' both describe the one Goddess: 'She who is both the higher and the lower'. Inside the compound parā takes its masculine stem para (puṃvadbhāva), which fuses with aparā by savarṇa-dīrgha.

Sanskrit componentIASTLiteral English meaning
परparasupreme, higher, transcendent
अपराaparānot supreme, lower, immanent — a- 'not' + parā

Spiritual significance The Muṇḍaka Upaniṣad (1.1.4) speaks of two knowledges, the higher (parā) and the lower (aparā); She is both, the transcendent and the manifest. In the Tantras Parāparā is also the middle of three levels (parā, parāparā, aparā).

Uncertain Read as 'both supreme and non-supreme' (karmadhāraya) or as 'the intermediate, Parāparā' (the middle of the Tantric triad).

(2) The whole is a bahuvrīhi describing Her: 'She whose form (rūpa) is truth, knowledge and bliss'; rūpa takes the feminine -ā to agree with Her. The three are not three qualities She possesses but Her very nature, which is why rūpa is used.

  • मूर्ताऽमूर्ता → मूर्ता + अमूर्ता (mūrtā + amūrtā) — savarṇa-dīrgha: ā + a → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ); the avagraha (ऽ) marks the absorbed initial a of the next name
  • अमूर्ताऽनित्यतृप्ता → अमूर्ता + अनित्यतृप्ता (amūrtā + anityatṛptā) — savarṇa-dīrgha: ā + a → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ); the avagraha (ऽ) marks the absorbed initial a of the next name

Three names hide in mūrtā'mūrtā'nityatṛptā: 813 mūrtā, 814 amūrtā, 815 anityatṛptā. Without the avagrahas the last could be misread as nityatṛptā.

brahmāṇī brahmajananī bahurūpā budhārcitā |

Where the names join in the śloka

  • प्रचण्डाऽऽज्ञा → प्रचण्डा + आज्ञा (pracaṇḍā + ājñā) — savarṇa-dīrgha: ā + ā → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ); the double avagraha (ऽऽ) marks the absorbed long ā of ājñā

ब्रह्मजननी is two names in Bhāskararāya's count, 822 brahma and 823 jananī, though it is often read as one ('Mother of Brahmā'); pracaṇḍā''jñā is 827 pracaṇḍā + 828 ājñā.

Not a compound.

Where the names join in the śloka

  • अयोनिर्योनिनिलया → अयोनिः + योनिनिलया (ayoniḥ + yoninilayā) — visarga after a vowel other than a or ā becomes r before a voiced sound, here y

Divide ayonir yoninilayā (894, 895): the r is the visarga of ayoniḥ. The two names are a deliberate paradox: without source, yet the abode of all sources.

Traditionally tattva is also read as Śiva, the highest principle, so that the name makes Her one with Him. Here tattvamayī is a single name; earlier in the hymn (425–427) Bhāskararāya divides the same letters into tat, tvam and ayī.

Complete meaning She who is worshipped by those of the right-hand path and those of the left

Spiritual significance Traditionally dakṣiṇa and adakṣiṇa are the right-hand (Vedic, samaya) and left-hand (vāma) modes of worship, and She receives both; the pair is also read as the learned and the unlearned, both of whom reach Her.

Uncertain Besides right-hand / left-hand ways, the pair is also read as the skillful and the unskillful (learned and unlearned); both readings rest on the same dvandva.

924दरस्मेरमुखाम्बुजाdara-smera-mukhāmbujā
Sandhi viccheda
  • मुखाम्बुजा → मुख + अम्बुजा (mukha + ambujā) — savarṇa-dīrgha: a + a → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ)
Samāsa vigraha

bahuvrīhi (over an inner karmadhāraya and an upamita-karmadhāraya)

दरम् स्मेरम् दरस्मेरम्; मुखम् अम्बुजम् इव मुखाम्बुजम्; दरस्मेरम् मुखाम्बुजम् यस्याः सा दरस्मेरमुखाम्बुजा
daram smeram darasmeram; mukham ambujam iva mukhāmbujam; darasmeram mukhāmbujam yasyāḥ sā darasmeramukhāmbujā

(1) dara-smera 'slightly smiling': the indeclinable dara 'a little' qualifies smera 'smiling'. (2) mukha-ambuja 'the face that is like a lotus': an upamita compound, the face compared to the lotus with the comparison word iva understood. (3) (1) qualifies (2), and the whole is a bahuvrīhi describing Her: 'She whose lotus-face is gently smiling'; ambuja takes the feminine -ā.

Sanskrit componentIASTLiteral English meaning
दरdaraslightly, a little — an indeclinable used adverbially
स्मेरsmerasmiling — √smi 'to smile' + the suffix -ra
मुखmukhaface
अम्बुजाambujālotus (lit. "water-born") — ambu 'water' + ja 'born'; with the feminine -ā of the bahuvrīhi

Complete meaning She whose lotus-face wears a gentle smile

Spiritual significance The slight smile is traditionally read as the outward sign of Her grace: it reassures the devotee and, in the Purāṇic account, is enough to destroy the demons.

925कौलिनीकेवलाkaulinī-kevalā
Sandhi viccheda
No sound change inside the name; the members stand as written.
Samāsa vigraha

karmadhāraya (one name made of two co-referential words); a tatpuruṣa reading is also given

कौलिनी च असौ केवला च कौलिनीकेवला; अथवा कौलिनीनाम् केवला कौलिनीकेवला
kaulinī ca asau kevalā ca kaulinīkevalā; athavā kaulinīnām kevalā kaulinīkevalā

Read as one name, kaulinī 'She of the Kula (the Kaula tradition)' and kevalā 'the Absolute, unmixed, alone' stand in apposition: 'the Kaula Goddess who is the Absolute'. A genitive reading, 'the Absolute for the Kaulas', underlies the traditional gloss that the followers of the Kaula way worship Her as pure consciousness. The words meet without sound change.

Sanskrit componentIASTLiteral English meaning
कौलिनीkaulinīShe of the Kula; the Goddess of the Kaula tradition — kaula 'pertaining to the kula' + the possessive -in, feminine -ī
केवलाkevalāalone, absolute, unmixed; pure consciousness without a second

Complete meaning She who, for the followers of the Kaula way, is the Absolute, pure consciousness

Spiritual significance Kula is the whole of manifest reality held together in Śakti; for the Kaula practitioner the Goddess of the Kula is herself kevala, the one consciousness without a second.

Uncertain The internal relation (apposition, or a genitive 'the Absolute for the Kaulas') is not settled; both are traditional and the meaning combines them.

Variants Some printings write कौलिनी केवला as two words; the 1,000-name count requires one name here (see the correction log).

Corrected in this edition कौलिनी केवला → कौलिनीकेवला. "कौलिनी केवला" → कौलिनीकेवला: counted as one name (925) in the 1,000; written as two words it reads as two names and breaks the count.

upapada-tatpuruṣa (over an inner karmadhāraya, itself over a nañ-tatpuruṣa and a karmadhāraya)

(1) an-arghya 'beyond price' (nañ-tatpuruṣa; na becomes an- before a vowel). (2) kaivalya-pada 'the state that is kaivalya' (karmadhāraya of identity). (3) (1) qualifies (2). (4) dāyinī 'giver' is the head and takes (3) as its object: 'She who gives the priceless state of liberation'.

Sanskrit componentIASTLiteral English meaning
अनर्घ्यanarghyapriceless, beyond all valuation — nañ (a-, an- before a vowel) + arghya 'to be valued'

Complete meaning She who bestows the priceless state of final liberation (kaivalya)

Spiritual significance Kaivalya, the isolation of the Self from all that is not the Self, is the highest goal; nothing can be paid for it, so it is Her gift alone.

(1) an-ullaṅghya 'not to be transgressed' (nañ-tatpuruṣa; na becomes an- before a vowel). (2) sarva-anullaṅghya 'not to be transgressed by anyone' (tṛtīyā-tatpuruṣa, the instrumental of the agent with the gerundive). (3) This qualifies śāsana 'command', and the whole is a bahuvrīhi: 'She whose command no one can transgress'.

Spiritual significance Even the gods, the sun, fire and wind act under Her command; the order of the cosmos is Her unbroken law.

(1) tri-pura 'the three cities, the three worlds' (dvigu). (2) tripura-sundarī 'the beauty of the three worlds', i.e. the most beautiful in them (saptamī-tatpuruṣa; a genitive reading gives the same sense). (3) śrīmatī 'glorious' qualifies her, reduced to śrīmat by puṃvadbhāva in the karmadhāraya: 'the glorious Tripurasundarī'.

Śloka 183

श्रीशिवा शिवशक्त्यैक्यरूपिणी ललिताम्बिका ।
एवं श्रीललितादेव्या नाम्नां साहस्रकं जगुः ॥ १८३ ॥

śrīśivā śivaśaktyaikyarūpiṇī lalitāmbikā |
evaṃ śrīlalitādevyā nāmnāṃ sāhasrakaṃ jaguḥ || 183 ||

Names in this śloka

  1. श्रीशिवा śrī-śivā
  2. शिवशक्त्यैक्यरूपिणी śiva-śakty-aikya-rūpiṇī
  3. ललिताम्बिका lalitāmbikā

The second half of this śloka, एवं श्रीललितादेव्या नाम्नां साहस्रकं जगुः, closes the hymn and contains no name. The names therefore fill 182½ ślokas.

The first half holds the last three names, 998–1000, ending on Her own name, Lalitāmbikā. The second half is not a name but the closing line: evaṃ śrīlalitādevyā nāmnāṃ sāhasrakaṃ jaguḥ, 'thus they sang the thousand names of the Goddess Śrī Lalitā'. jaguḥ is the perfect, 3rd plural, of √gai 'to sing'; traditionally the singers are the Vāgdevīs (Vaśinī and the others), who composed the hymn at Her command. Inside the line, devyā is devyāḥ (genitive) with its visarga dropped before the voiced n of nāmnām, and evam, nāmnām and sāhasrakam show m → ṃ before a consonant. text.json prints श्रीललिता देव्या with a space; it is one genitive compound, śrīlalitā-devyāḥ, 'of the Goddess Śrī Lalitā'.

śrī 'auspicious, glorious' stands in apposition to śivā 'the auspicious one, Śiva's consort': 'the auspicious Śivā'. The members meet without sound change.

श्रीśrīauspicious, glorious; Śrī

Spiritual significance She is Śivā, the power of Śiva and auspiciousness itself; the next name declares Śiva and Śakti to be one.

999शिवशक्त्यैक्यरूपिणीśiva-śakty-aikya-rūpiṇī
Sandhi viccheda
  • शक्त्यैक्य → शक्ति + ऐक्य (śakti + aikya) — yaṇ: i → y before an unlike vowel (Pāṇini 6.1.77 iko yaṇ aci)
Samāsa vigraha

possessive in -in over a karmadhāraya, a ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa and an itaretara-dvandva

शिवः च शक्तिः च शिवशक्ती; शिवशक्त्योः ऐक्यम् शिवशक्त्यैक्यम्; शिवशक्त्यैक्यम् एव रूपम् शिवशक्त्यैक्यरूपम्; तत् अस्याः अस्ति इति शिवशक्त्यैक्यरूपिणी
śivaḥ ca śaktiḥ ca śivaśaktī; śivaśaktyoḥ aikyam śivaśaktyaikyam; śivaśaktyaikyam eva rūpam śivaśaktyaikyarūpam; tat asyāḥ asti iti śivaśaktyaikyarūpiṇī

(1) śiva-śakti 'Śiva and Śakti' (itaretara-dvandva). (2) śivaśakti-aikya 'the oneness of Śiva and Śakti' (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa). (3) That oneness is identified with rūpa 'form', and the possessive -in (feminine -iṇī) makes the whole describe Her: 'She whose form is the union of Śiva and Śakti'.

Sanskrit componentIASTLiteral English meaning
शिवśivaŚiva
शक्तिśaktiŚakti, power
ऐक्यaikyaoneness, union — abstract noun from eka 'one'
रूपिणीrūpiṇīhaving the form — rūpa 'form' + -in, feminine

Complete meaning She who is the union of Śiva and Śakti in one form

Spiritual significance The whole of Śrīvidyā rests on this non-duality: Śiva without Śakti cannot act, Śakti without Śiva has no ground; Kāmeśvara and Kāmeśvarī are one.

Corrected in this edition शिवशक्तैक्यरूपिणी → शिवशक्त्यैक्यरूपिणी. शिवशक्तैक्य → शिवशक्त्यैक्य: śakti + aikya gives śakty-aikya (yaṇ sandhi); the y was missing.

1000ललिताम्बिकाlalitāmbikā
Sandhi viccheda
  • ललिताम्बिका → ललिता + अम्बिका (lalitā + ambikā) — savarṇa-dīrgha: ā + a → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ)
Samāsa vigraha

karmadhāraya

ललिता च असौ अम्बिका च ललिताम्बिका
lalitā ca asau ambikā ca lalitāmbikā

Lalitā and ambikā 'Mother' are co-referential: 'Lalitā, the Mother'. ambikā is the head; the two simply meet in savarṇa-dīrgha.

Sanskrit componentIASTLiteral English meaning
ललिताlalitāLalitā: 'She who plays', the lovely one — √lal 'to play, sport', past participle, feminine
अम्बिकाambikāmother — ambā + -ka, feminine

Complete meaning She who is the divine Mother Lalitā

Spiritual significance The thousand names end with Her own name: Lalitā, whose play is the universe, and Ambikā, the Mother to whom every name has been addressed.

Colophon

इति श्रीब्रह्माण्डपुराणे उत्तरखण्डे श्रीहयग्रीवागस्त्यसंवादे श्रीललितासहस्रनामस्तोत्रकथनं सम्पूर्णम् ॥

iti śrībrahmāṇḍapurāṇe uttarakhaṇḍe śrīhayagrīvāgastyasaṃvāde śrīlalitāsahasranāmastotrakathanaṃ sampūrṇam ||

Thus ends the narration of the Śrī Lalitā Sahasranāma Stotra, in the dialogue of Śrī Hayagrīva and Agastya, in the Uttara-khaṇḍa of the Brahmāṇḍa Purāṇa.

ajā-jaitrī		Typographical. अजाजेत्री → अजाजैत्री (jaitrī, victorious: vṛddhi ai); the verse reads अजाजैत्री.

gurū-maṇḍala-rūpiṇī

guru-maṇḍala-rūpiṇī		Typographical. गुरूमण्डल → गुरुमण्डल (guru: short u).

Śloka 183: names 998–1000 (श्रीशिवा शिवशक्त्यैक्यरूपिणी ललिताम्बिका) with its closing half.StructuralThe names fill 182½ ślokas; the half-śloka of names 998–1000 is completed by the closing half. Half-line translations64 half-lines whose English did not give one clause per name (e.g. śloka 17, second half: "Has no birth; Heroic", which belongs to no name in that line).Every half-line translation is now generated from the meanings of exactly the names in that half-line, in order.StructuralMeanings had drifted between half-lines and ślokas. Generating them removes the drift and keeps them in step with the names.

Word-by-word tables713 names had a table built from a generic dictionary (e.g. ābāla-gopa glossed "beetle"; stūyamānātma as one unit); 287 names had none.All 1,000 names have a table written from the grammar: one unit per row in its underlying form, each with its literal meaning.InterpretiveThe tables must follow sandhi and samāsa, not string matching.
Page header182 Shlokas183 Shlokas (182½ of names)StructuralCounts the half-śloka of names 998–1000.
Śloka 183, second halfएवं श्रीललिता देव्या … (śrīlalitā devyā)एवं श्रीललितादेव्या … (śrīlalitādevyā)Orthographicśrīlalitā-devyāḥ is one compound in the genitive ("of the Goddess Śrī Lalitā"); the space made śrīlalitā read as a separate nominative. devyā is devyāḥ with its visarga dropped before n.
