A.3 English meanings rewritten (45)

Meanings that were wrong, belonged to another name, or did not follow the grammar. Meanings that were only tidied (spelling, IAST for ITRANS) are not listed; 574 were tidied and 381 kept as they were.

NamePrevious meaningNowReason
16She who wears a musk mark on Her forehead which shines like the spot in the moonShe whose musk tilaka looks like the dark mark on the moon of Her faceThe previous text missed the grammar: mukha-candra is the moon that is Her face (rūpaka), and -ābha means 'resembling'; the mark is dark like the moon's spot, it does not 'shine like' it.
32She whose neck is resplendent with a gem-studded necklace with a locket made of pearlShe who is adorned with a jewelled necklace, a cintāka and swaying pearls'neck' is not in the name and lola 'swaying' was not translated; the name lists three ornaments joined by anvitā, rather than a necklace with a locket made of pearl.
50She whose body is worthy of worshipShe whose every limb is faultlessanavadya means 'faultless, blameless', not 'worthy of worship'; the previous meaning did not follow from the word.
56She who is the Mistress of the most auspicious (or prosperous)She who is the sovereign of the glorious city (Śrīpura)The previous meaning broke off ('the Mistress of the most auspicious (or prosperous)') and omitted nagara 'city'.
83She whose many powers are extolled by brahmA, viShNu, shiva and other godsShe whose glory is extolled by Brahmā, Upendra (Viṣṇu), Mahendra (Indra) and the other godsMahendra is Indra, not Śiva; the names of the gods are now given as the compound names them, in IAST.
86She who from Her neck to Her waist is of the form of theShe whose form from below the throat down to the waist is the middle kūṭa (the kāmarāja-kūṭa) of the PañcadaśīThe previous meaning broke off ('is of the form of the'); it is completed from the compound: the region is the middle kūṭa.
113She who is unattainable through imagination or thoughtShe who is attained through contemplation (bhāvanā)The previous meaning followed the alternative division bhāvanā + agamyā ('unattainable'); the division bhāvanā-gamyā, already used in the old word-split and parallel to bhakti-gamyā (119), is followed here, and the alternative is recorded as uncertain.
126She who gives happinessShe who is the consort of Śaṅkara (Śiva)The long ā (vṛddhi) shows that śāṅkarī is derived from Śaṅkara: 'of Śaṅkara, His consort'. 'She who gives happiness' is the etymology of śaṅkara and is kept in the significance.
133She who stays unattached, bound to nothingShe who is without stain'stays unattached, bound to nothing' did not follow the compound; añjana is a dark stain, so nirañjanā is 'stainless'.
203She who pervades every living and non-living thingShe who is everything-mayī means 'consisting of'; the name says She is made of everything, not that She 'pervades' it.
207She who is shiva's shaktiShe who is Manonmanī, the state in which the mind transcends itself'Śiva's śakti' is one traditional identification but not what the name says; the name is the yogic state beyond the mind, and the identification is kept under significance.
209She who has the immeasurable bodyShe who is the great Goddess'immeasurable body' is a commentarial gloss on mahā, not the meaning of the name; it is kept under significance.
225She who is the object of worship even by the greatest of yogisShe who is the sovereign of the great lords of yogaThe name says She is the sovereign (īśvarī) of the great masters of yoga; 'object of worship' is an inference, not the grammar.
226She who is worshipped by the great Tantras such as kulArnava and jnAnArnavaShe who is the great Tantra'Worshipped by the great Tantras' is not in the name; it describes Her as the great Tantra, parallel to names 227–228. The examples are kept under significance.
241She who has a beauty that does not wax or waneShe whose form is beautiful'A beauty that does not wax or wane' is a commentarial gloss drawn from the moon names; the name itself says 'beautiful form'. The gloss is kept under significance.
271She who protects and rules everythingShe who is the Sovereign, Īśvarī'Protects' is not in the name; īśvarī is 'sovereign', and in this sequence the consort-power of Īśvara, deity of the fourth act (concealment).
279She who protects those who worship HerShe who is the Blessed One, possessed of all six excellences'Protects those who worship Her' is not in the name; bhagavatī means 'possessing bhaga', the six excellences (name 277).
363She who is the embodiment of truth (which is indicated by the word 'tat')She who is the implied meaning (lakṣyārtha) of the word 'tat' (That)'the embodiment of truth' missed the technical term: lakṣyārtha is the meaning reached by implication (lakṣaṇā), as opposed to the literal meaning (vācyārtha).
364She who is of the nature of the pure intelligence. She who is the cause of knowledgeShe whose nature is consciousness alone, one undivided essence'She who is the cause of knowledge' is not in the name, and ekarasa 'one undivided essence' was not translated.
367She who is of the nature of unmanifested consciousness or of unmanifested brahmanShe whose form is inward-turned consciousnesspratyak means 'inward-turned', not 'unmanifested'; the name speaks of consciousness as the inner Self.
418She who is the mAyA that has transformed itself as the power of creationShe who is the power that becomes the insentient worldThe previous gloss ('the māyā that has transformed itself as the power of creation') gave commentary as translation; the name says 'the power of the insentient'. The māyā reading moves to significance.
448She who is the ultimate truthShe who is endowed with well-being (svasti)'the ultimate truth' is interpretation, not the meaning of the word; svasti-matī is 'possessed of svasti, well-being'. The interpretation is kept under significance.
454She who has rolling eyes. separate name कामरूपिणी - She who is in the form of love in womenShe who takes the form of love (kāma) in women, the restless-eyedThe old meaning cut the name in two ('rolling eyes' + a separate kāmarūpiṇī). In the 1,000-name count it is one name, and the meaning now follows the compound.
466She who creates upheaval in the mindShe who stirs the stillness into creation'creates upheaval in the mind' is not the traditional sense; kṣobha here is the creative stirring.
471She who is the goddess worshipped by spiritual adeptsShe who is the sovereign of the siddhas, the perfected adepts'worshipped by spiritual adepts' changed the relation; the compound says She is the sovereign (īśvarī) of the siddhas.
481She who is the deity of the organ of touch (skin)She who abides in the skinThe name places Her in the skin as a bodily tissue (dhātu); 'deity of the organ of touch' turned it into the sense of touch.
552She who guards Her devotees from allShe who wards off every kind of deathThe previous text was truncated ('guards Her devotees from all') and omitted death (mṛtyu), the object of the name.
638She who is the cause of the universeShe whose womb is golden, the source of the world (as Hiraṇyagarbha)The old meaning ('the cause of the universe') stated only an interpretation; the name says Her womb is golden, recalling Hiraṇyagarbha.
651She who knows the truth of the physical universeShe who is the knowerThe old meaning ('knows the truth of the physical universe') added an object the name does not have; vijñātrī is simply 'the knower'.
666She who is the aggregate of all existing thingsShe whose form is the Bhūman, the boundless Plenitude'the aggregate of all existing things' takes bhūman only as 'multitude'; the name's classic source is the Upaniṣadic Bhūman, the Infinite. The aggregate reading is kept in the significance.
674She who is predominantly sAttvicShe who is Brāhmaṇī, belonging to Brahman'predominantly sāttvic' is an interpretation, not what the word says; it is kept in the significance and the meaning now gives the word.
686She who protects all the dominionsShe to whom sovereignty is dearvallabha means 'dear, beloved', not 'protecting'; the name says the realm is dear to Her (or She is its beloved).
687She who has a compassion that captivates everyoneShe whose compassion shines forthrājat is 'shining, resplendent', not 'captivating'.
689She who is the embodiment of the prosperity of the worldShe who is the Fortune (Lakṣmī) of the kingdomrājya is 'kingdom, sovereignty', not 'the world'.
712She who is the symbol 'I' (Other versions show 711/712 as sAdhvI eventhough it is a repetition.)She who is the syllable ī (kāmakalā)The old meaning ('the symbol I') mixed in an editorial remark; the name is the vowel ī, and the note on other versions moved to variants.
723She who is free from all limitationsShe who is independent, subject to none'free from all limitations' belongs rather to name 708; svatantrā is 'self-ruled, independent'.
728She who is the consciousness in brahmanShe who is the digit (kalā) of consciousness'the consciousness in brahman' did not render kalā; the name is the kalā, digit or subtle power, of consciousness.
756She who killed chaNDa, muNDa and other asurasShe who slew the demons Caṇḍa and Muṇḍa'and other asuras' is not in the name, which names exactly two demons; ITRANS spelling replaced.
772She who is difficult to controlShe who cannot be assailed or overpoweredādharṣa is 'assailing, overpowering'; 'difficult to control' is not its sense.
792She who is immersed in a state of steady wisdomShe who is wholly intent on sāmarasya, the perfect equipoise of Śiva and Śakti'Steady wisdom' does not translate sāmarasya, the technical term for the union in one flavor of Śiva and Śakti (or of the individual and the Supreme).
796She who has a desirable formShe who assumes any form at will'Desirable form' takes kāma as an adjective; the compound means 'form at will' (or 'the form of Kāma').
821She who is the tail that is brahman; the support for allShe who is Brahmāṇī, the creative power of BrahmāThe older rendering 'the tail that is Brahman' gives only a commentarial interpretation as though it were the translation; the name itself is the feminine of Brahmā/Brahman.
830She who is manifested in the form of the universeShe whose form is manifest'In the form of the universe' is not in the name; the bahuvrīhi says only that Her form is manifest.
853She who transcends the state of peaceShe whose very nature is the kalā beyond peace (śāntyatītā)The name does not say She transcends peace in general: it names the fifth kalā, śāntyatītā, as Her nature.
905She who is seated in the baindava (spot between the eyebrows) chakraShe whose seat is the bindu, the central point of the ŚrīcakraThe baindava place is the central point (bindu) of the Śrīcakra, not 'the spot between the eyebrows', which is the ājñā.

Appendix B — Variants and open questions

B.1 Textual variants

NameReading adoptedVariantNote
40मुकुट (mukuṭa)मकुट (makuṭa)Both are recognised spellings of "crown". The source's śloka text read mukuṭa, its name list makuṭa.
46शिञ्जान (śiñjāna)सिञ्जान (siñjāna)Both appear in print; the śloka text of the source read siñjāna, its name list śiñjāna. śiñjāna follows the root (√śiji). Flagged for review against a printed Saubhāgyabhāskara.
107तडिल्लता (taḍillatā)तटिल्लता (taṭillatā)taḍit and taṭit both mean lightning. The source reads taḍit in both its śloka text and its name list; the independent copy reads taṭit in its nāmāvalī.
511बन्धिन्यादि (bandhinyādi)बन्दिन्यादि (bandinyādi)The attendant śaktis of Rākiṇī. The source and the independent copy's stotra read bandhinī; that copy's nāmāvalī reads bandinī. Flagged for review.
547बन्धुरालका (bandhurālakā)बर्बरालका (barbarālakā)The source's śloka text read bandhurālakā (as does the independent copy); its name list read barbarālakā, which many numbered lists print. bandhura "wavy", barbara "curly": the sense is the same. Flagged for review against a printed Saubhāgyabhāskara.
879सुधासृतिः (sudhāsṛtiḥ)सुधास्रुतिः (sudhāsrutiḥ)"Stream of nectar"; the source carried both, separated by a slash. sṛti (flow) is the śloka text's reading.
235चतुःषष्टि (catuḥṣaṣṭi)चतुष्षष्टि (catuṣṣaṣṭi)Also 236, 237. Both spellings are correct (Pāṇini 8.3.36); one is used throughout.
Dhyāna 2mayūkhaiḥ ahammayūkhair ahamSandhi across the pāda boundary is optional; the source does not apply it, many editions do.
Dhyāna 4japavidhau smared ambikāmjapavidhau smarāmy ambikām"Let one remember" / "I remember": both are current.

B.2 Interpretations marked uncertain (129)

Each is flagged at the name itself. Listed here for scholarly review.

  • 1 श्रीमाता — Two compound analyses are current: karmadhāraya ('the auspicious Mother') and ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa ('Mother of Śrī/Lakṣmī'). The meaning follows the first; the second is given in the samāsa note.
  • 4 चिदग्निकुण्डसम्भूता — Ablative ('arisen from') and locative ('born in') analyses of the last member are both current.
  • 25 शुद्धविद्याङ्कुराकारद्विजपङ्क्तिद्वयोज्ज्वला — The identification of śuddhavidyā with the sixteen-syllabled mantra (and of the 32 teeth with it) is widely reported from the commentarial tradition; its exact source wording was not confirmed here.
  • 26 कर्पूरवीटिकामोदसमाकर्षिदिगन्तरा — The relation of samākarṣin to digantara admits two readings: the quarters draw in (are pervaded by) the fragrance, as analysed here, or the fragrance draws the beings of every quarter to Her, the usual paraphrase, which takes digantara by metonymy for those who dwell there.
  • 32 रत्नग्रैवेयचिन्ताकलोलमुक्ताफलान्विता — The exact form of the cintāka is not certain: it is taken as a gold collar-necklace or as the pendant (locket) of the jewelled necklace. On the second reading the analysis is 'the jewelled necklace with its pendant, and swaying pearls'.
  • 37 अरुणारुणकौसुम्भवस्त्रभास्वत्कटीतटी — aruṇāruṇa may be read as 'red as the dawn' (upamāna, as analysed) or as the color word doubled for emphasis, 'deep red, red upon red'.
  • 41 इन्द्रगोपपरिक्षिप्तस्मरतूणाभजङ्घिका — Translators take indragopa here either as the scarlet insects themselves, scattered over the quiver, or as red gems of their color set around it; the comparison of the calves to Kāma's quiver is not in doubt.
  • 59 महापद्माटवीसंस्था — mahā may qualify the forest ('the great lotus forest') or the lotuses ('the forest of great lotuses'); both readings are current and the sense is the same.
  • 62 कामाक्षी — Several analyses are current: kāma as 'lovely' (the meaning given), as 'love, desire' dwelling in Her eyes, and the traditional kā + mā + akṣī (Sarasvatī and Lakṣmī as Her eyes).
  • 68 चक्रराजरथारूढसर्वायुधपरिष्कृता — The compound can also be read with ārūḍha qualifying āyudha, 'equipped with all the weapons placed on the Cakrarāja chariot', parallel to names 69–70 where ārūḍha qualifies the following member. The meaning given follows the usual reading.
  • 86 कण्ठाधःकटिपर्यन्तमध्यकूटस्वरूपिणी — The first part, kaṇṭhādhaḥ-kaṭiparyanta, can be analysed adverbially or as a bahuvrīhi qualifying an understood 'part of the body'; the relation to the head is therefore stated in sense (locative) rather than as one fixed samāsa type.
  • 90 कुलामृतैकरसिका — eka can be taken with kulāmṛta ('the kula-nectar alone') or with rasikā (eka-rasikā 'having one delight'); the sense is the same.
  • 93 कुलान्तस्था — The division kula-anta-sthā 'abiding at the end (or the inner part) of kula' is also possible; the reading antar + sthā is followed here.
  • 97 समयान्तस्था — As with name 93, the division samaya-anta-sthā ('abiding at the end of samaya') is also possible.
  • 106 सुधासाराभिवर्षिणी — sudhā-sāra 'the essence of nectar' is also a possible division; 'downpour' suits abhivarṣiṇī 'raining down' and is followed here.
  • 109 महासक्तिः — The division mahā + sakti 'great attachment' is also possible; maha 'festival' + āsakti 'attachment' is followed here because it explains the festive union of the traditional gloss.
  • 113 भावनागम्या — Both divisions are traditional: bhāvanā-gamyā 'attainable through contemplation' and bhāvanā-agamyā 'unattainable through (mere) imagination'. The Devanagari is the same either way.
  • 207 मनोन्मनी — The junction mano + unmanī is not regular sandhi and the analysis of this technical term varies (some read manas + unmanī as a karmadhāraya, 'the mind that has become unmanī'); the meaning follows the common yogic sense.
  • 237 महाचतुःषष्टिकोटियोगिनीगणसेविता — Whether mahā- qualifies the number, the yoginīs or their hosts is not decided by the grammar; the sense hardly changes.
  • 258 स्वपन्ती — By Pāṇini (7.1.80–81) the feminine participle of the class-2 root svap (svapiti) would be svapatī; svapantī follows the thematic inflection (svapati) found in epic usage. The text reads svapantī and the metre is the same either way.
  • 264 सृष्टिकर्त्री — Pāṇini 2.2.15 restricts compounding a genitive with an agent noun in -tṛ; compounds like sṛṣṭi-kartṛ are nevertheless standard in usage and are usually explained as a general genitive (śeṣa-ṣaṣṭhī).
  • 281 उन्मेषनिमिषोत्पन्नविपन्नभुवनावली — A bahuvrīhi ending in an ī-stem like āvalī would by Pāṇini 5.4.153 normally take the suffix -ka (…āvalīkā); the name keeps -āvalī, which is common in such poetic compounds.
  • 303 हृद्या — Two derivations are current: 'dear to the heart' (4.4.95) and 'being in the heart'; the meaning gives both.
  • 309 रञ्जनी — The root allows two senses, 'one who colors (reddens)' and 'one who delights'; the meaning gives the second, the significance the first.
  • 313 रमा — The earlier rendering added Sarasvatī; that rests on a commentarial derivation I could not confirm, so it is left out.
  • 316 रतिप्रिया — Bahuvrīhi ('to whom Rati is dear') and ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa ('dear to Rati') are both possible; rati may also be the common noun 'delight'.
  • 320 रमणलम्पटा — ramaṇa can be the beloved (Śiva) or the act of love-play itself ('eager for love-play'); the meaning follows the first.
  • 322 कामकलारूपा — kāmakalā is analysed both as 'the digit of Kāma' (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa) and as 'Kāma and Kalā' (dvandva).
  • 328 कलालापा — The fused ā allows kalā 'art' + ālāpa as well: 'She whose talk is of the arts'. The usual reading takes kala 'sweet'.
  • 332 वामनयना — vāma means both 'beautiful' and 'left'; the meaning takes the first.
  • 342 क्षेत्रेशी — The name may mean 'ruler of the field' (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa) or 'wife of Kṣetreśa, Śiva' (puṃyoga feminine); both are current.
  • 345 क्षेत्रपालसमर्चिता — The story of the infant Kṣetrapāla is traditionally told on this name; I could not confirm its Purāṇic source, so it is not attributed.
  • 351 वामकेशी — Read as a bahuvrīhi ('beautiful-haired') or as the consort of Vāmakeśa, Śiva; the meaning takes the first.
  • 367 प्रत्यक्चितीरूपा — The long ī of citī is not the regular form of citi; it is analysed here as a lengthening of citi (some take it as metrical).
  • 368 पश्यन्ती — The bodily seat of each level of speech is placed differently in different texts (paśyantī at the svādhiṣṭhāna in some, at the navel in others); the sequence parā–paśyantī–madhyamā–vaikharī itself is undisputed.
  • 370 मध्यमा — The bodily seat of each level of speech is placed differently in different texts (paśyantī at the svādhiṣṭhāna in some, at the navel in others); the sequence parā–paśyantī–madhyamā–vaikharī itself is undisputed.
  • 374 कृतज्ञा — kṛtajñā means both 'knowing what is done' and 'grateful'; both are given.
  • 375 कामपूजिता — The allusion to the Kāmagiri pīṭha (reading 'worshipped at Kāma[giri]') is traditional but not in the grammar of the name.
  • 392 श्रीकण्ठार्धशरीरिणी — For an exact half Pāṇini's rule (2.2.2 ardhaṃ napuṃsakam) puts ardha first; here, as often in later usage, it follows in a genitive compound.
  • 405 शिवदूती — The bahuvrīhi ('whose messenger is Śiva', as in the Devī Māhātmya story) and the ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa ('messenger of Śiva') are both current.
  • 407 शिवमूर्तिः — 'whose form is Śiva' (bahuvrīhi) and 'auspicious form' (karmadhāraya) are both possible.
  • 410 शिवपरा — 'devoted to Śiva' (bahuvrīhi) and 'beyond Śiva' (pañcamī-tatpuruṣa) are both current; the meaning follows the first.
  • 411 शिष्टेष्टा — iṣṭā may be from √iṣ ('dear to the righteous') or √yaj ('worshipped by the righteous'); a bahuvrīhi 'to whom the righteous are dear' is also given by some.
  • 415 मनोवाचामगोचरा — Whether manovācām agocarā is one compound with the genitive retained or two words read as a single name is not settled; the meaning is the same.
  • 422 सन्ध्या — The word is derived from sam + √dhyai ('meditation') or from sandhi 'junction' (sam + √dhā); both are traditional.
  • 424 तत्त्वासना — A second analysis takes āsana as an agent noun from √ās 'to sit': tattveṣu āste 'She who abides in the tattvas'. The bahuvrīhi ('whose seat is the tattvas') is the more natural reading of the compound.
  • 427 अयी — The sense of ayī is not settled. The common interjection of address is ayi with a short i; the long ī here is read either as that particle lengthened or as a feminine form, and the commentarial derivation could not be confirmed here. The rendering follows the usual reading as a call of address.
  • 438 कुरुकुल्ला — The derivation of the name is obscure, and the place Kurukullā holds in Śrīnagara is described differently in the sources; the old note that she resides in the kuruvinda ruby could not be confirmed.
  • 448 स्वस्तिमती — The reading of svasti as 'imperishable being' is traditional; the exact source in the commentaries could not be confirmed here.
  • 452 तेजोवती — The usual Pāṇinian derivation keeps the s of tejas before a possessive suffix (Pāṇini 1.4.19 tasau matvarthe), giving tejasvatī; tejovatī, with the s treated as a word-end, is the attested form of the name.
  • 454 लोलाक्षीकामरूपिणी — lolākṣī can also be taken as an epithet of the Goddess herself ('the restless-eyed one, whose form is Kāma'); the rendering follows the reading of lolākṣī as 'women'.
  • 456 हंसिनी — The possessive suffix allows several senses — 'having the haṃsas (great yogins) as Her own', 'having the haṃsa (swan or breath-mantra)' — and the tradition gives more than one.
  • 460 नलिनी — nalinī also means a lotus pond, and is the name of one of the streams of the Gaṅgā; which sense is primary is a matter of interpretation.
  • 464 कालकण्ठी — The name can also be read directly as a bahuvrīhi of Her own ('She whose throat is dark'), or with kālakaṇṭha in the sense 'whose throat is sweet-voiced'; the reading as Śiva's consort is the usual one.
  • 466 क्षोभिणी — What She stirs is not named; the creative agitation of prakṛti is the usual reading, and agitation of the mind of Śiva or of devotees is also given.
  • 469 वामदेवी — Two analyses are current: the consort of Vāmadeva, followed here, and 'the lovely goddess' (vāmā devī).
  • 472 सिद्धविद्या — The reason the pañcadaśī is called siddha is given traditionally as above; the exact commentarial source could not be confirmed here.
  • 476 आरक्तवर्णा — ā- can also intensify ('deep red'); the rendering 'rosy, reddish' is the usual one.
  • 479 वदनैकसमन्विता — The order face-one is unusual. It is read here as a karmadhāraya with the numeral placed second (compare 487 and 496, where dvaya and traya are nouns, 'a pair', 'a triad'); the sense is not in doubt.
  • 484 डाकिनीश्वरी — Karmadhāraya ('She who is Ḍākinī, the sovereign') and ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa ('sovereign of the ḍākinīs') are both possible; the parallel names 494, 503, 520 and 534 (…ambāsvarūpiṇī) favor the first.
  • 491 कालरात्र्यादिशक्त्यौघवृता — śaktyaugha requires the member augha, a by-form of ogha 'flood, host' (śakti + ogha would give śaktyogha); the sense is not affected.
  • 526 हरिद्रान्नैकरसिका — eka-rasikā may also be read as 'having a single taste, absorbed in one relish'; the sense is the same.
  • 545 पुलोमजार्चिता — That Śacī's worship secures Indra's rule is a traditional reading; no single source for it was confirmed here.
  • 547 बन्धुरालका — The reading itself: this edition follows the verse text (bandhurālakā) where the old name list read barbarālakā; which of the two Bhāskararāya's text adopts could not be confirmed here. The sense is the same either way.
  • 556 कात्यायनी — Purāṇic accounts differ on whether She was born in Kātyāyana's hermitage or first worshipped by him; the derivation from Kata is standard grammar.
  • 572 पराशक्तिः — Phrase or compound: the retained feminine parā and the verse's spacing point to two words in agreement (no samāsa); in later usage Parāśakti is also treated as a fixed compound title.
  • 573 परानिष्ठा — Phrase or compound, as with name 572: the feminine parā is kept, so the name is read as two words in agreement.
  • 587 श्रीषोडशाक्षरीविद्या — The composition of the Ṣoḍaśī (which syllable completes the Pañcadaśī, and where it is placed) differs between lineages; the significance gives the commonest account.
  • 589 कामकोटिका — koṭi has several senses (portion, extremity, ten million), and the name is also read as 'She who dwells at Kāmakoṭi', the pīṭha at Kāñcī. The meaning follows the reading of Kāma as a part of Her.
  • 590 कटाक्षकिङ्करीभूतकमलाकोटिसेविता — kaṭākṣa may be taken in the genitive ('handmaids of Her glance') or the instrumental ('made handmaids by Her glance'); the image is the same.
  • 603 गुरुमूर्तिः — Two compound analyses: bahuvrīhi ('whose form is the guru') and karmadhāraya ('the weighty, awesome form'). The meaning follows the first.
  • 610 प्रतिपन्मुख्यराकान्ततिथिमण्डलपूजिता — tithimaṇḍala may be taken as the agent (instrumental, 'by the circle of days', i.e. their deities) or as the time (locative, 'on each of the days'); both readings are current.
  • 612 कलानाथा — Read as a ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa ('mistress of the kalās'); the sense 'She who is the moon' (kalānātha) is also current.
  • 622 क्लीङ्कारी — Two analyses: 'maker of klīṃ' (upapada-tatpuruṣa) and 'She who is the syllable klīṃ' (klīṅkāra + feminine -ī); traditionally She is both its source and its form.
  • 624 गुह्या — Derived from √guh 'to hide' (gerundive) or from guhā 'cave' ('dwelling in the cave of the heart'); both are traditional.
  • 626 त्रिपुरा — Two derivations: tri + pura 'three cities' (bahuvrīhi) and tri + purā 'before the three' (the traditional reading). The meaning gives both.
  • 630 त्र्यक्षरी — Which three syllables are meant is explained in more than one way (Oṃ, the Bālā mantra, the three kūṭas).
  • 638 स्वर्णगर्भा — The old meaning gave an interpretation ('the cause of the universe'); the literal bahuvrīhi and its echo of Hiraṇyagarbha are given here. Bhāskararāya's own gloss of this name was not confirmed.
  • 639 अवरदा — The derivation from √do 'to cut' is the traditional one; -dā could also be read from √dā 'to give' ('She who gives even to the lowly'). The name is avaradā, not varadā: the avagraha in the verse marks the elided a.
  • 655 योग्या — yogya means both 'fit, worthy' and 'to be attained by yoga'; the meaning follows the second, the significance mentions the first.
  • 666 भूमरूपा — bhūman can mean 'the Infinite' (Chāndogya 7.23–24) or 'manyness, the aggregate'; both are current for this name.
  • 674 ब्राह्मणी — Several readings are current: 'of the nature of Brahman', 'predominantly sāttvic' (the brāhmaṇa as sattva), and the Śakti of Brahmā; the source of the sāttvic gloss could not be confirmed.
  • 677 बलिप्रिया — bali may also be read from balin 'the strong': 'She who loves the strong' (those strong in devotion and self-mastery).
  • 683 शोभनासुलभागतिः — Not a compound: the adjectives keep their feminine -ā, which they would lose inside a karmadhāraya (śobhana-sulabha-gati); the name is three nominatives in apposition, counted as one name. gati can be 'goal' or 'path'.
  • 684 राजराजेश्वरी — rājarāja may be 'kings of kings' (emperors) or Kubera, the king of the yakṣas; both readings are current.
  • 686 राज्यवल्लभा — vallabha also means 'lord, overseer' in some lexicons, which would support 'protector of kingdoms'; the bahuvrīhi 'to whom sovereignty is dear' and the tatpuruṣa 'beloved of the realm' are the plain readings.
  • 695 दीक्षिता — The participle is passive ('consecrated'), but the name is commonly explained as 'She who initiates', taking dīkṣitā as 'possessed of dīkṣā'; both are current.
  • 706 गुहाम्बा — The fused ā allows guha 'Skanda' or guhā 'cave'; both readings are traditional.
  • 711 साधु — Bhāskararāya's own gloss of sādhu could not be checked against a printed Saubhāgyabhāskara; 'equanimity' (the earlier meaning) may reflect it.
  • 712 ई — The kāmakalā reading is the Śrīvidyā one; single-syllable lexicons also give ī as a name of Lakṣmī. Bhāskararāya's exact gloss could not be checked against a printed text.
  • 714 कुलोत्तीर्णा — kula has several traditional senses here — the senses, the Kaula path, the family of the knower–knowing–known; the reading as 'the senses' follows the earlier meaning.
  • 715 भगाराध्या — bhaga can be taken as the sun's disc or as the trikoṇa of Śrīcakra; the meaning follows the first.
  • 725 दक्षिणामूर्तिरूपिणी — The sense of dakṣiṇā in the proper name is explained variously ('facing south', 'gracious', 'skilled'); 'facing south' is the usual one.
  • 728 चित्कला — ṣaṣṭhī ('a digit of consciousness') and karmadhāraya ('consciousness as subtle power') readings are both possible.
  • 733 नन्दिविद्या — Which form of the mantra is meant by Nandividyā, and its place among the worshippers' vidyās, could not be confirmed against a printed commentary.
  • 754 अपर्णा — The name has two analyses: apa + ṛṇa 'free of debt' (the meaning given) and a + parṇa 'without (even) a leaf', the classical name of Pārvatī.
  • 785 मार्ताण्डभैरवाराध्या — The place of Mārtāṇḍa Bhairava in Her city follows the usual account; the exact enclosure could not be confirmed against a printed text.
  • 786 मन्त्रिणीन्यस्तराज्यधूः — Pāṇini 5.4.74 adds the compound-final -a to a compound ending in dhur (…-dhura); the name keeps the bare dhūḥ, a usage also found in epic and Purāṇic Sanskrit. Noted, not a text concern: the verse and the metre support dhūḥ.
  • 790 परापरा — Read as 'both supreme and non-supreme' (karmadhāraya) or as 'the intermediate, Parāparā' (the middle of the Tantric triad).
  • 793 कपर्दिनी — The feminine of kapardin can mean 'wife of Kapardin' (the usual reading) or 'She who herself wears the kaparda braid'.
  • 794 कलामाला — Ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa ('the garland of the arts') and bahuvrīhi ('whose garland is the arts') readings are both current.
  • 796 कामरूपिणी — Three readings are current: 'taking form at will', 'having the form of Kāma/Kāmeśvara', and 'Goddess of Kāmarūpa'.
  • 804 पुष्करा — puṣkara has many senses (lotus, water, sky, the tīrtha Puṣkara); the gloss 'nourishing' rests on a traditional etymology from √puṣ rather than on regular grammar.
  • 809 परात्परा — Whether parātparā is an aluk compound or a two-word phrase written together is a matter of analysis; the meaning is the same.
  • 815 अनित्यतृप्ता — The śloka's continuous text mūrtāmūrtānitya… could also be divided amūrtā + nityatṛptā 'ever satisfied'; the edited text marks the a of anitya with an avagraha, following the traditional division.
  • 821 ब्रह्माणी — The traditional interpretation through 'brahma pucchaṃ pratiṣṭhā' rests on a derivation that could not be confirmed; the plain grammatical sense is given as the meaning.
  • 838 मुकुन्दा — The derivation muku 'liberation' + dā 'giving' is a traditional etymology (nirukti), not regular grammar.
  • 839 मुक्तिनिलया — The feminine ending admits two analyses: an adjectival ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa ('the abode of liberation') and a bahuvrīhi ('whose abode is liberation').
  • 847 तलोदरी — Two readings are current: 'whose waist is flat (slender)' and 'in whose belly are the talas, the lower worlds'.
  • 855 गगनान्तस्था — anta can be read as 'limit' (beyond the sky) or 'interior' (within space); both readings are current.
  • 860 अकान्ता — aka 'pain, sin' is a rare word and the analysis aka + antā is the traditional one; the śloka's sandhi kāṣṭhā'kāntā fixes the initial a, so a reading kāntā 'beloved' is not available here.
  • 875 त्रिपुरमालिनी — As a proper name its internal analysis is not fixed; the vigraha given is grammatical, not a traditional gloss.
  • 895 योनिनिलया — Read as 'the abode of all sources' or as 'She who dwells in the yoni (the central triangle)'.
  • 903 कल्या — kalya has several senses (able, healthy, auspicious; also 'dawn'), and traditional glosses differ; the rendering combines the main ones.
  • 912 सव्यापसव्यमार्गस्था — savya is mostly 'left' but is occasionally used for 'right' in ritual contexts; the name covers both paths either way.
  • 916 धीरा — The sense 'giver of wisdom' depends on the traditional analysis dhī + √rā; the ordinary meanings are 'wise' and 'steadfast'.
  • 923 दक्षिणादक्षिणाराध्या — Besides right-hand / left-hand ways, the pair is also read as the skillful and the unskillful (learned and unlearned); both readings rest on the same dvandva.
  • 925 कौलिनीकेवला — The internal relation (apposition, or a genitive 'the Absolute for the Kaulas') is not settled; both are traditional and the meaning combines them.
  • 940 परामोदा — The usual division is para + āmodā; parā + modā is also possible, with the same sense.
  • 945 वामकेश्वरी — The sense of vāmaka (the left-hand way, or 'beauty') is variously explained.
  • 946 पञ्चयज्ञप्रिया — Which five sacrifices are meant (śrauta rites, the five mahāyajñas, or Āgamic five) differs between explanations.
  • 971 सुवासिन्यर्चनप्रीता — suvāsinī-arcana may mean worship OF suvāsinīs (the Śrīvidyā rite of suvāsinī-pūjā) or worship BY them; the first is followed.
  • 972 आशोभना — The verse string can be cut prītā + āśobhanā or prītā + śobhanā with identical sound; Bhāskararāya's division (āśobhanā) is followed.
  • 976 त्रिपुराम्बिका — Genitive ('Mother of the three cities') and appositional ('Tripurā the Mother') analyses are both current.
  • 978 त्रिपुराश्रीवशङ्करी — Tripurāśrī as the fifth-enclosure deity and as 'the fortune of the three worlds' are both traditional readings.
  • 983 त्रिखण्डेशी — Trikhaṇḍā as the tenth mudrā, or the three kūṭas of the Pañcadaśī mantra: both are traditional.
  • 985 अम्बा — triguṇāmbā can also be read as one word, 'the Mother of the three guṇas'; the 1,000-name count follows Bhāskararāya's two names.
  • 994 आबालगोपविदिता — The outer link of the avyayībhāva to the participle viditā is loose; it may also be read as an instrumental, 'known by (all) down to children and cowherds'.
  • 996 श्रीचक्रराजनिलया — The compound can also be read śrī + cakrarāja, 'the glorious king of cakras'; both name the Śrīcakra.

Appendix C — Batch consistency reports

The analysis was done in batches of ten ślokas. After each, a check proved that the batch lists exactly the names of its ślokas in order, that every IAST string is the exact transliteration of its Devanagari, and that every name has its sandhi, samāsa, word table, meaning and significance.

BatchŚlokasNamesReport
11–101–26Checked all 26 names of ślokas 1–10 against text.json: sandhi at every member junction (and at visible prefix junctions such as ud + jvalā), a layered samāsa analysis with vigraha-vākyas written word by word in pausa form, and the meanings against that analysis. One word boundary was wrong in the old reading form and split (15: vibhrājad-alika, not vibhrāja-dalika) and one member was misidentified (26: āmoda 'fragrance', not moda); name 16's meaning missed the face-as-moon compound and was replaced. No problem was found in the Sanskrit text; no external sandhi joins names in these ślokas.
211–2027–48Checked all 22 names of ślokas 11–20 against text.json: sandhi at every member junction (including prefix junctions sam + lāpa, ud + neya, sam + channa), a layered samāsa analysis with pausa-form vigraha-vākyas, and the meanings against that analysis. Two members were misidentified in the old split (35: ādhāratā 'being the support', not dhāratā 'stream'; 41: indragopa is one word, a scarlet insect, not Indra + 'beetle') and one member boundary was wrong (32: phala belongs to muktāphala 'pearl'); name 32's meaning was replaced. No error was found in the Sanskrit; name 40's recent correction to mukuṭa is sound, but the earlier makuṭa is a recognized by-form and is recorded as a variant, not a typo. No external sandhi joins names in these ślokas.
321–3049–77Checked all 29 names of ślokas 21–30 against text.json: sandhi at every member junction (and the prefix junctions sam + sthā, adhi + sthita, puras + kṛtā), a layered samāsa analysis with pausa-form vigraha-vākyas, and the meanings against that analysis. Name 50's meaning was wrong (anavadya is 'faultless', not 'worthy of worship') and 56's was truncated; both were replaced. Several old splits misplaced boundaries (64: stūyamāna | ātma-vaibhava; 71: the goddess-name Jvālāmālinikā cut in two; 67: koṭibhiḥ + āvṛtā is two words, so the name is a phrase, not one compound). No error was found in the Sanskrit; the only external sandhi is sarvāruṇā + anavadyāṅgī in śloka 21.
431–4078–111Checked all 34 names of ślokas 31–40 against text.json (the end of the Bhaṇḍāsura war, the three kūṭas of the subtle form, and the kula/kuṇḍalinī section): sandhi at every member and visible prefix junction, layered samāsa analysis with pausa vigrahas, and each meaning against that analysis. Several members were misidentified in the old splits: 82 śūnyakā is Bhaṇḍa's city Śūnyaka, not 'void'; 106 is sudhā + āsāra 'downpour', not sāra 'essence'; 109 has dental s (āsakti 'attachment'), not śakti 'power'; 101 cut through maṇipūra. Name 83's meaning (Mahendra glossed as Śiva) was replaced and 86's truncated meaning completed. No problem was found in the Sanskrit; no external sandhi joins names in these ślokas.
541–50112–192Checked all 81 names of ślokas 41–50 against text.json: Bhavānī and the names of devotion, then the long series of nirguṇa names built on nis 'without' (132–187), whose every prefix form (nir, niṣ, niś, nis, niḥ, nī) is explained as sandhi, followed by the 'without X / destroyer of X' pairs.
